This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The overarching task is executing/auditing the SFCC-236 "Product Card Shared Component" build for the Zimmermann PWA Kit, on branch `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (branched from `develop`, never pushed to origin, no PR open). Work has spanned: (a) reading and correcting the build plan document (`plan.md`) and postbuild audit record (`postbuild.md`), both living outside the app repo at `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/`; (b) running nine rounds of the `zimmerMANNPostBuild` skill's audit-fix loop, each a genuinely fresh `zm-orchestrator`/`zm-tester` pass per the skill's own "re-audit is a fresh pass" rule; (c) executing numerous specific, Marcel-directed fixes dispatched via `zm-implementer` sub-agents (never done directly by me except one small, fully-pre-specified docblock correction); (d) a running commitment to verify every claim against real evidence (code, live Figma via MCP tools, live Storybook via browser MCP tools until they disconnected) rather than trusting docs, plans, or CodeRabbit at face value; (e) strict adherence to AGENTS.md's Hard Rules — especially never committing/pushing/opening a PR without the developer's explicit request in the current prompt, and the "implementer writes only what it's told, the skill (me) does all staging and committing" discipline established throughout. Most recently, Marcel explicitly said "hold off on the PR, we have some work to do" and then drove a sequence of detailed component/story audits and fixes (One Size styling, slide indicator spec-check, arrows/remove-button hover behavior vs. AC, placeholder image colors, was/now price coverage), each requiring investigation before action and each fix dispatched to `zm-implementer` before being verified and committed by me.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Zimmermann PWA Kit override architecture: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/` with `index.tsx`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`, `<name>.css.ts` per component.
   - Chakra UI multi-part recipes via `useMultiStyleConfig`, registered in `theme/components/index.ts` (Tier 2).
   - Tier 1/2/3/4 file protection system (`frozenFiles.md`, `protectedFiles.md`, CODEOWNERS) and the "verified-session exception" for Tier 1 (checking `gh api user`/team membership before requiring separate confirmation).
   - `CARD_SLOT` (10 named `data-card-slot` attribute constants) and `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` (`'@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)'`) — both defined once in `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/zimmProductCardShared.ts` (the ONE legitimate shared file, at `ui-kits/` root — justified because the organism's recipe must select into sibling molecules' DOM for CSS-only hover reveals, a deliberate no-React-hover-state perf decision for 60+ PLP tiles).
   - `VARIATION_CONFIG` in `zimmProductCard/index.tsx` — a declarative, per-variation (`home`/`plp`/`wishlist`) boolean-flag table (`showBag`, `showSizeChips`, `showBadge`, `showHoverImageSwap`, `hoverHidesPrice`, `hoverRevealsPrice`, `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`, `hoverRevealsNotifyMe`, `sizeSelectorUnavailable`, `hideBagOnMobile`) driving the organism's render with zero `switch`/`if` on variation.
   - The established cross-sibling hover-reveal pattern in `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s `root` part: rules nested inside `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]`, using `` [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.x}"]`] `` and the `&:focus-within` twin, to reveal/hide content across Media/Content slots from the organism's own recipe.
   - `zm-implementer`/`zm-tester`/`zm-orchestrator`/`zm-scorer`/`zm-planner` — custom Agent subagent_types for this project's build loop; `zm-implementer` "writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope," never stages/commits.
   - `zimmerMANNPreBuild`/`zimmerMANNBuild`/`zimmerMANNPostBuild`/`zimmerMANNReview`/`zimmerMANNDevImprover`/`zimmerMANNRevImprover`/`zimmerMANNSprinter`/`zimmerMANNDevOps` — custom Skills (found at `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, mirrored in `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/`) implementing this project's whole planning/build/review/ops lifecycle.
   - Figma MCP tools (`mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_metadata`, `get_design_context`, `get_screenshot`) — used extensively and successfully throughout for direct design verification; requires loading the `figma:figma-design-to-code` skill before `get_design_context`.
   - Browser automation MCP tools (`mcp__Claude_Browser__*`) — used for live Storybook verification (screenshots, DOM/ARIA inspection via `javascript_tool`, click/keyboard simulation) until this MCP server disconnected mid-session (ambient system reminder confirmed `claude-in-chrome` disconnected).
   - `data:image/svg+xml` data-URI images as Storybook fixtures — confirmed these are isolated external resources that CANNOT resolve parent-page CSS custom properties (`var(--...)`); fill values must be literal hex.
   - `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s styling hierarchy (textStyle > var(--zimm-*) > component theme config > sx > scoped scss), the "no bare token key" rule enforced by `recipeGuards.test.ts`, and the discovered/proven coverage gap in that same test's exhaustive prop-combination walk (only varies 5 fixed prop names, misses this feature's custom flags — confirmed via controlled mutation test, reported to Marcel as out-of-scope-to-fix here).
   - `npm run audit:tokens` (`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`) excludes `*.stories.tsx` and `*.test.ts(x)` from its raw-hex/px/rem scan.
   - Git safety: never amend without explicit user request (I violated a commit-message accuracy once, Marcel said "fix" it, I then amended since nothing was pushed); `git filter-branch --msg-filter` used once (with explicit re-authorization after an auto-mode classifier block) to strip `Co-Authored-By` trailers from unpushed commits.
   - CodeRabbit CLI (`coderabbit`/`cr` command) — `cr review --light --base develop` vs. the deeper `cr review --base develop` (no `--light`); this project's own documented distrust ("CodeRabbit has run as low as 1-in-6 correct on this repo") requiring independent verification of every finding before acting.
   - WCAG 2.2 AA (target size 2.5.8, focus visibility) — recurring accessibility verification theme (24px minimum hit areas, `role="group"`/`aria-label` patterns, `:focus-within` parity with `:hover`).

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/plan.md` — the build plan; repeatedly read and edited to add §4f (badge reinstatement), correct §3's manifest (Tier 1/2 disclosure, `zimmProductCardShared.ts` relocation history, `productCardFixtures.ts`'s full lifecycle: created→citation-fixed→un-extracted, manifest count corrections). Currently reflects the true, final state of all these decisions.
   - `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/postbuild.md` — the postbuild audit record; has "Round 1" through "Round 9" sections, each documenting a fresh audit pass, findings, verdicts, and fixes, per the skill's explicit "write it down... a clean audit that left no record is indistinguishable from one that never ran" requirement. Contains the final, comprehensive PR title/body draft (title: `feat(ui-kits): SFCC-236 product card shared component — atoms, molecules, and organism`).
   - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/zimmProductCardShared.ts` — the one legitimate shared file (relocated here from inside the organism's folder in Round 3), exports `CARD_SLOT` (10-key object) and `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`. Untouched throughout the later un-extraction of its sibling `productCardFixtures.ts`.
   - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts` — the organism's cross-component hover-reveal recipe; most recently modified (via `zm-implementer`) to add:
     ```ts
     [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },
     [`&:focus-within [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },
     ```
     inside the existing `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` block (unconditional, no `VARIATION_CONFIG` flag), matching the exact pattern already used for `hoverRevealsPrice`/`hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector`/`hoverRevealsNotifyMe`. A new docblock point 6 was added documenting this.
   - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` — the `carousel` part's `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: {display:'flex'}` sub-block was REMOVED entirely (now `display:'none'` unconditionally at this level; the reveal lives only in the organism's recipe now). The `close`/`arrowButton`/`indicatorWrapper` parts were confirmed correct and untouched. Earlier in the session, this file's `oneSize`-equivalent... (N/A, that's a different file) — this file's `close` part is unconditional `display:'flex'` (confirmed correct per AC+Figma, left untouched per explicit instruction).
   - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` — I directly edited (not via `zm-implementer`) its module docblock (~lines 99-107) to correct stale language claiming both arrows and the indicator are "gated by the recipe's own CSS media query." New text:
     ```
     * Touch paging is native CSS scroll-snap at every breakpoint; arrows are a progressive
     * enhancement over the same scroll container, never a second, independent mechanism. Arrows and
     * the slide indicator are mutually exclusive by pointer capability
     * (`(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`) and never both interactively visible at once. Both
     * exist in the DOM at all times, gated via CSS rather than a JS `window.matchMedia` check —
     * matching the "keep in DOM, hide via CSS" precedent `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` already uses for its
     * off-page swatches — so server and client render identically (no hydration mismatch) and
     * neither affordance depends on `matchMedia`, which jsdom (this component's own Vitest
     * environment) does not implement. The two affordances differ in *where* that CSS lives, though:
     * the indicator is fully gated by this recipe's own media query. The arrows are not — this
     * recipe only ever sets them to `display: none`; the actual reveal (`display: flex`, on

Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)

- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';
3	import { CARD_SLOT, HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY } from '../../zimmProductCardShared';
4	
5	/**
6	 * Same hover-capable-pointer gate `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already establishes for its own
7	 * arrows/indicator split — now a shared import from `zimmProductCardShared.ts` rather than each
8	 * file's own module-private copy, so the two can't silently drift. Governs the price <->
9	 * size-selector swap below, so both composed children's hover treatments engage together off the
10	 * exact same media feature, on this shared root.
11	 */
12	
13	/**
14	 * A viewport-width gate, unrelated to `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above — governs the PLP-only bag-icon
15	 * mobile hide (Fix D, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) below. Same `breakpoints` token and mobile-
16	 * first `min-width` direction `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own `root` padding step already
17	 * uses, imported from the same place, so the two files can't drift on what "desktop" means here.
18	 */
19	const DESKTOP_QUERY = `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`;
20	
21	type ZimmProductCardStyleProps = {
22	  /** Home only — see VARIATION_CONFIG in index.tsx. Price is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer
23	   *  type by default and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card. */
24	  hoverRevealsPrice?: boolean;
25	  /** PLP + Wishlist — price is visible by default (Content's own natural rendering; no override
26	   *  needed for that half) and hides only once a hover-capable pointer hovers the card. */
27	  hoverHidesPrice?: boolean;
28	  /** PLP + Wishlist — the size-chip picker is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type by default
29	   *  and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card, in the same
30	   *  media-query gate as the price swap above so both engage together. */
31	  hoverRevealsSizeSelector?: boolean;
32	  /** Fix C — true whenever ZimmProductCardContent actually mounted a notify-me button
33	   *  (`isUnavailable && onNotifyMe`, computed once in index.tsx as `showNotifyMe`). Unlike the two
34	   *  flags above, the "hidden by default" half lives INSIDE `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`, not outside it
35	   *  — see docblock point 4: a touch pointer must see notify-me unconditionally (confirmed via
36	   *  every Mobile Unavailable Figma reference), where price/the size-selector do the opposite. */
37	  hoverRevealsNotifyMe?: boolean;
38	  /** Fix C — true for a PLP/Wishlist card that would normally hover-swap to the size-selector
39	   *  (`config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector`) but is out of stock. Unlike every other flag here, this
40	   *  is not a pointer-type concern at all: the size-chip wrapper stays hidden permanently, in
41	   *  every state, on every device — see docblock point 4. */
42	  sizeSelectorUnavailable?: boolean;
43	  /** Fix D — PLP only (`VARIATION_CONFIG.plp.hideBagOnMobile` in index.tsx). A viewport-width
44	   *  concern, not a pointer-type one: hidden below `breakpoints.md`, visible from it up — see
45	   *  docblock point 5. */
46	  hideBagOnMobile?: boolean;
47	};
48	
49	/**
50	 * Recipe for the product-card organism (ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard) — composes
51	 * ZimmProductCardMedia (Step 4) and ZimmProductCardContent (Step 5) with no styling of its own
52	 * for either child. This recipe's entire job is the cross-component concerns neither child can
53	 * own by itself:
54	 *
55	 *   1. THE STRETCHED-LINK OVERLAY. ZimmProductCardContent's `nameLink` renders the one real `<a>`
56	 *      in the whole composed tree. Its `::after` is stretched to `inset: 0` against THIS
57	 *      component's own `root` — the nearest positioned ancestor. Confirmed by reading
58	 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly: neither its `root` nor `nameRow`, `nameLink`, or
59	 *      any other part sets `position` anywhere in that file, so nothing between the `<a>` and
60	 *      this `root` intercepts the containing-block chain. (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root`
61	 *      IS `position: relative`, but Media is a *sibling* of Content under this organism's root,
62	 *      never an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it has no bearing on this chain.)
63	 *   2. LIFTING EVERY OTHER INTERACTIVE CONTROL above that overlay — a z-index higher than the
64	 *      overlay's own (left unset), or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first.
65	 *      Three separate, single-selector keys rather than one comma-joined selector: verified via
66	 *      this project's own installed Stylis (v4.2.0 — the same engine Emotion/Chakra invoke at
67	 *      runtime, confirmed by direct compilation) that a comma-separated list DOES distribute this
68	 *      recipe's generated class across every branch correctly, but three plain keys need no such
69	 *      verification to trust at a glance and are each individually addressable from a test. Only
70	 *      ONE of the three (`content` buttons) also adds `position: relative` — that element is
71	 *      `position: static` by default in its own component recipe, so a positioned ancestor is
72	 *      needed for z-index to apply at all. `close` and `carousel` are the two exceptions:
73	 *      `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own recipe already positions each of them directly (`close` via
74	 *      `position: absolute, top: 0, right: 0`; `carousel` via `position: absolute, top: 50%, ...`),
75	 *      so each needs (and gets) only the z-index bump here:
76	 *        - `close` — a competing `position` value previously declared alongside it had HIGHER
77	 *          specificity than Media's own rule (this rule is a class+attribute descendant selector;
78	 *          Media's is a single class) and silently won the cascade, knocking the remove button out
79	 *          of its pinned top-right corner into normal document flow (Fix 1). See the inline
80	 *          comment at that key below and index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe block for the proof.
81	 *        - `carousel` — Fix 3 (found during the manual real-browser check performed after the
82	 *          round-2 Scorer PASS, which explicitly flagged that check as still outstanding, not by
83	 *          any automated pass). The lift rule used to target
84	 *          `'[data-card-slot="carousel"] button'` — the two arrow BUTTONS individually, each given
85	 *          its own `position: relative, zIndex: 1` — identical in shape to the `content button`
86	 *          rule above, and every jsdom test passed. A real click in a real browser still landed on
87	 *          the overlay, not the arrow. Root cause: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `carousel` part
88	 *          sets `transform: translateY(-50%)` (to vertically centre the arrow row against `slide`),
89	 *          and `transform` unconditionally creates a NEW stacking context on that element,
90	 *          regardless of its `position`/`z-index`. That traps each arrow button's `zIndex: 1`
91	 *          *inside* the carousel wrapper's own stacking context — it only wins ordering battles
92	 *          against the *other* arrow button, never against anything outside `carousel` (like the
93	 *          content overlay), because the whole `carousel` box is itself just an ordinary
94	 *          z-index:auto participant one level up — and, being earlier in DOM order than
95	 *          `[data-card-slot="content"]`, it lost. Moving the lift to the `carousel` WRAPPER itself
96	 *          (already `position: absolute` from Media's own recipe, so only `zIndex: 1` is needed
97	 *          here, same as `close`) fixes this: the wrapper's own stacking context — not one buried
98	 *          inside it — is what gets compared against the overlay, and it wins outright, carrying
99	 *          both arrow buttons above the overlay with it. This is exactly the gap
100	 *          index.test.tsx's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock warns about — jsdom resolves no
101	 *          stacking contexts at all, so this shipped past every automated check and was only
102	 *          found by a real click in a real browser. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 3" describe block.
103	 *   3. THE HOVER-REVEAL SWAP between price and the PLP/Wishlist size-selector (and Home's
104	 *      hidden-by-default price), gated by the same `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` query
105	 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already uses for its own arrows/indicator split. Each reveal
106	 *      rule fires on `:hover` OR `:focus-within` on this same root (Fix 2 rework below) — `:hover`
107	 *      alone would leave every reveal permanently unreachable by keyboard on a hover-capable
108	 *      device, since `display: none` removes the unconditional-state element from the tab order
109	 *      entirely and nothing but a real pointer hover could ever have revealed it.
110	 *   4. NOTIFY-ME'S HOVER GATE (Fix C, found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit against the
111	 *      real Figma Default+Hover Unavailable instances for all three variations, desktop AND
112	 *      mobile). Three behaviours confirmed together, all different from point 3 above:
113	 *        - `isUnavailable` suppresses the PLP/Wishlist size-selector swap entirely (index.tsx
114	 *          AND-s `hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` with `!isUnavailable` before they
115	 *          ever reach this recipe) — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price
116	 *          stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own `hoverRevealsPrice` is
117	 *          untouched by this — its Unavailable Hover reference still reveals price normally.
118	 *        - Suppressing that swap is not, by itself, enough to reproduce the reference: with no
119	 *          hide/reveal pair of its own, the size-chip wrapper falls back to Content's natural
120	 *          (visible) default and would show permanently — briefly shipped exactly that way mid-fix
121	 *          and caught by re-checking the real render against Figma, which shows size chips hidden
122	 *          in BOTH states when unavailable, not merely "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
123	 *          (index.tsx: `config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && isUnavailable`) carries that permanent
124	 *          hide as its own unconditional rule below — deliberately outside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`
125	 *          entirely, since unlike everything else here this isn't a pointer-type distinction at
126	 *          all: every device sees it hidden, full stop.
127	 *        - Notify-me itself is hover-gated the OPPOSITE way round from price/the size-selector:
128	 *          hidden by default and revealed on hover **only inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`**, not
129	 *          unconditionally. Every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it appearing only on
130	 *          hover; every Mobile Unavailable reference (Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so
131	 *          whatever it shows is the only state a touch pointer ever sees) shows it plainly with no
132	 *          reveal needed. Putting the "hidden by default" half outside the media query — matching
133	 *          point 3's own structure literally — would have made notify-me permanently invisible on
134	 *          touch, since a touch pointer never matches `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` and so could never
135	 *          trigger the `:hover`/`:focus-within` half either.
136	 *   5. THE BAG ICON'S PLP-ONLY MOBILE HIDE (Fix D, same SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit). A genuinely
137	 *      different axis from points 3-4 above: `DESKTOP_QUERY` is a **viewport-width** media query
138	 *      (`min-width`), not `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`'s pointer-capability one — a large touch tablet and
139	 *      a small hover-capable laptop window need to agree with Figma's own Desktop/Mobile split by
140	 *      width, not by input method. Figma's PLP/PDP Mobile Card-content instance
141	 *      (`40002163:41479`) has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`; Desktop's own PLP
142	 *      instance and Wishlist's Mobile instance (`40002187:58472`) both leave it visible — so this
143	 *      is `hideBagOnMobile`, one boolean `index.tsx` derives from TWO separate per-variation
144	 *      config fields (`hideBagOnMobile` proper, PLP's own unconditional rule; and
145	 *      `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable`, Fix G's narrower Wishlist-only-when-out-of-stock rule —
146	 *      see index.tsx's own docblock and `bagHiddenOnMobile` derivation), not a blanket rule. This
147	 *      recipe only ever sees the one already-combined boolean — it has no opinion on which of the
148	 *      two reasons produced it. Hidden unconditionally by default (mobile-first, matching
149	 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own padding step direction), then shown again from
150	 *      `DESKTOP_QUERY` up as `display: 'flex'` — not `'block'` — since that is the actual display
151	 *      type `bagWrapper`'s own recipe uses for its icon-centring; this selector's specificity
152	 *      (a class + two attribute selectors) beats Content's single class either way, so restoring
153	 *      the wrong display value would have silently flattened that centring rather than merely
154	 *      failing to apply — the inverse of point 3's hover-reveal shape, but the same "start from
155	 *      the narrowest/most restrictive case, widen from there" idea.
156	 *   6. THE CAROUSEL ARROW REVEAL (behavioural fix, confirmed against the Jira AC — "when on
157	 *      desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear" — and live Figma: the Carousel
158	 *      element is `hidden="true"` on every Default-state instance checked and visible only on
159	 *      the matching Hover-state instance, for both PLP and Wishlist). Unlike points 3-4 above,
160	 *      this reveal is **unconditional** inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` — not gated behind a
161	 *      `ZimmProductCardStyleProps` flag — because the arrows behave identically across every
162	 *      variation (Home/PLP/Wishlist) whenever a card has more than one image; there is no
163	 *      `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry for it and this fix does not add one. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s
164	 *      own `carousel` part used to reveal itself unconditionally inside its own
165	 *      `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` block — a device-CAPABILITY check, not an actual-hover check —
166	 *      which made the arrows visible permanently on any hover-capable device instead of only
167	 *      while genuinely hovering/focusing the card. That sub-block is now removed entirely from
168	 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`; the `:hover`/`:focus-within` pair here is the only reveal
169	 *      path left, the same mechanism point 3 already established for price/the size-selector.
170	 *      Purely additive to the existing `carousel` z-index lift in point 2 above — that lift
171	 *      already handles stacking once the arrows are visible; this handles visibility itself.
172	 *
173	 * Parts: only `root` is declared. Everything above is a nested descendant selector inside
174	 * `root`'s own style object (targeting the composed children's `data-card-slot` attributes), not
175	 * a separate Chakra part — `index.tsx` never reads anything off `useMultiStyleConfig` but
176	 * `styles.root`, so `recipeParts.test.ts`'s declared-vs-read reconciliation needs nothing more.
177	 *
178	 * `zIndex: 1` below is this file's one deliberately unnamed magic number — accepted per
179	 * .claude/rules/conventions.md's own exception ("0, 1, -1 in obvious idiomatic uses"): it is the
180	 * standard "one level above the default/auto stacking layer" value, used identically at each of
181	 * the three lift points, and the stretched-link overlay is deliberately left with no z-index of
182	 * its own rather than pinned to a specific lower number — so the two sides only ever need to be
183	 * *some* value vs a *higher* one, never a specific pair.
184	 */
185	export const ZimmProductCard = {
186	  parts: ['root'],
187	
188	  baseStyle: ({
189	    hoverHidesPrice,
190	    hoverRevealsPrice,
191	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
192	    hoverRevealsNotifyMe,
193	    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
194	    hideBagOnMobile,
195	  }: ZimmProductCardStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
196	    root: {
197	      position: 'relative',
198	      width: '100%',
199	
200	      // 1. Stretched-link overlay — see docblock point 1. Deliberately no z-index of its own
201	      // (stays at the default/auto stacking layer), so every control lifted in point 2 below
202	      // reliably paints above it regardless of DOM order.
203	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] a::after`]: {
204	        content: '""',
205	        position: 'absolute',
206	        inset: 0,
207	      },
208	
209	      // 2. Every genuinely-interactive control sits above the stretched overlay. A plain `button`
210	      // type-selector under the relevant data-card-slot root reaches every control uniformly —
211	      // none of them declare their own data-card-slot, and none needs one: Content's bag button,
212	      // its notify-me button, and every ZimmSizeChip button nested inside its own sizeChips
213	      // wrapper are all real <button> descendants of [data-card-slot="content"].
214	      // Fix 1 (Scorer rework round 1): NO position value here. ZimmProductCardMedia's own
215	      // `close` recipe part already sets `position: 'absolute', top: 0, right: 0` on this exact
216	      // element (that's how the remove button pins to the image's top-right corner). This rule's
217	      // `.css-root [data-card-slot="close"]` descendant+attribute selector has HIGHER
218	      // specificity than Media's own single-class rule, so a competing `position` value declared
219	      // here would win the cascade and knock the button out of its pinned position into normal
220	      // flow — which is exactly what shipped here before this fix. The element is already
221	      // positioned (by Media's own recipe), which is all `zIndex` needs to take effect; no
222	      // `position` re-declaration was ever necessary. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe
223	      // blocks for the object-shape and real-DOM/getComputedStyle proof.
224	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.close}"]`]: {
225	        zIndex: 1,
226	      },
227	      // Fix 3 — zIndex only, on the carousel WRAPPER, not on each arrow `button` inside it. See
228	      // docblock point 2 above for why lifting the buttons individually left them unclickable in
229	      // a real browser (a `transform`-induced stacking context on this wrapper trapped their own
230	      // zIndex) despite passing every jsdom test.
231	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
232	        zIndex: 1,
233	      },
234	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] button`]: {
235	        position: 'relative',
236	        zIndex: 1,
237	      },
238	
239	      // 3. Hover-reveal swap — see docblock point 3. The unconditional (outside-media-query)
240	      // half of each flag below is what makes a touch/no-hover pointer see the *default* state
241	      // permanently: it never matches HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY at all, so whichever rule fired outside
242	      // it (or the total absence of one) is the only state that pointer type ever sees.
243	      //
244	      // `hoverRevealsPrice` (Home) is deliberately NOT here, unlike `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`
245	      // below it — see Fix E in the [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY] block: Home's price must stay visible
246	      // unconditionally on a touch pointer, the opposite of what an unconditional hide here would
247	      // do.
248	      ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
249	        // PLP/Wishlist: size-selector starts hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type...
250	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
251	      }),
252	      // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Unconditional and permanent, on every device: an
253	      // out-of-stock item never gets the size-selector, in any state, so this is the only rule

content.text:
The hover-out bug is confirmed by reading the recipe: the carousel reveal uses `&:focus-within` on the card root, and clicking an arrow button gives it real DOM focus in most browsers — `:focus-within` then stays true (arrows stay visible) until focus moves elsewhere, regardless of mouse position. The fix is `:has(:focus-visible)` instead of `:focus-within` — it only matches keyboard-triggered focus, not mouse-click focus, so hover-out will correctly hide the arrows while Tab-based keyboard access still works. `:has()` is fully covered by this project's browserslist (iOS 17+, Android 14+, last 4 ChromeAndroid — all far past `:has()`'s 2022/2023 support baseline), and no code here uses it yet, so this is a first instance, not an established pattern.

Reading the same file, I can see this exact same `:focus-within`-sticks-after-click mechanism is built into 4 other reveals in this recipe (price show/hide, size-selector reveal, notify-me reveal) — all keyed off the same shared root, so clicking a size chip or the notify-me button would reproduce the identical stuck-open symptom.

content.text:
I don't have live access to re-check this right now — no Jira/Atlassian tool is connected this session, and the Figma tool needs a file key/URL I don't currently have in context (it wasn't preserved through the earlier context compaction). So this is a review of the record already established earlier in this session, not a fresh independent re-check. Here's what that record shows, sourced from what's actually quoted in the code and commit `72ee2a9`:

**Arrows — aligned, and that's exactly why the fix happened.**
- AC: *"when on desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear"* — appear on an actual hover.
- Figma: the Carousel element is `hidden="true"` on every Default-state instance and visible only on the matching Hover-state instance, confirmed for both PLP and Wishlist.
- The old code contradicted both: it gated arrows on `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` alone — a device-capability check ("can this device hover") not an actual-hover check — so arrows were permanently visible on any mouse-capable device. That's the bug commit `72ee2a9` fixed by moving the reveal to `&:hover`/`&:focus-within` on the card root.
- No discrepancy between AC, Figma, or the fix's intent.

**Remove ("x") button — also aligned, deliberately untouched.**
- AC has no "on hover" qualifier for it.
- Figma shows it visible in both the Default and Hover Wishlist instances.
- Correctly left unconditional. No conflict.

**Where AC/Figma/comments are silent — the hover-out and keyboard-focus mechanics.**
Neither the AC nor Figma say anything about *un*-revealing on hover-out, and Figma has no keyboard-focus variant to check against at all (it only models Default/Hover). The `:focus-within` addition — and now the `:has(:focus-visible)` fix for the stuck-open bug you just found — exist purely to satisfy this project's own WCAG 2.2 AA target (AGENTS.md), not because any design or AC source asked for them. So there's no conflict here either, just nothing to check against: it's an implementation-level accessibility decision layered on top of a spec that doesn't address it.

I don't have the exact comment-thread text anymore to re-quote verbatim (it was pasted earlier and dropped out with context compaction), but at the time I cross-checked AC+Figma+comments together before proceeding, and didn't find anything in the comments that conflicted with the hover-only arrows / always-visible remove-button conclusion — if it had, I'd have stopped and flagged it per AGENTS.md rather than shipping a fix. If you want a fresh, live re-verification against Figma right now, paste a link and I'll check it directly.

The `:has(:focus-visible)` fix is done and verified. Summary:

**What landed** (3 files: `zimmProductCard.css.ts`, `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`, `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`):
- All 5 `:focus-within` → `:has(:focus-visible)` swaps confirmed by direct grep (price show/hide, size-selector, notify-me, carousel arrows) — the arrows will now correctly drop out on hover-out unless a real keyboard Tab put focus there.
- Docblocks/comments rewritten under a new "Fix H" label explaining why, on all 6 spots I'd specified.
- One genuine deviation the implementer found and fixed properly: running the test file in full (not isolation) exposed that this project's jsdom+nwsapi stops treating a later plain `.focus()` call as `:focus-visible`-satisfying once an earlier test in the same file drove a real `userEvent.click()`. Fixed by switching that test to `await user.tab()` — a real simulated keypress, arguably a more honest test than the imperative `.focus()` it replaced. Verified deterministic across 4 repeated full-file runs.

Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. There are two files OUTSIDE this repo, at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/plan.md` and `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/postbuild.md`, which are the build plan and postbuild audit record for the "SFCC-236 Product Card Shared Component" feature (organism: `ZimmProductCard`, composing molecules `ZimmProductCardMedia` and `ZimmProductCardContent`). Read-only investigation — no edits anywhere.

I'm about to redesign this component's Storybook stories from scratch, driven by real product variants/states as required by the Jira ACs, Figma designs, and Jira comments — rather than the current "per-Figma-node coverage folder" structure. I need a complete, citation-backed inventory of every distinct visual/behavioral state this component family is supposed to support, as already established during the original build. Read BOTH files in full and extract every distinct state/variant/condition mentioned, each with its citation. Specifically pull out:

1. **The three variations** (`home`, `plp`, `wishlist`) and exactly what differs between them per variation — badge presence, hover-image-swap, price behavior on hover, size-selector behavior on hover, notify-me, bag visibility on mobile, remove/wishlist-x button, anything else called out.
2. **Every "Fix" (numbered 1-6 and lettered A-H if present)** described in either file — a one-line summary of each, what state/condition it governs, and its citation (AC quote, Figma node ID, or "Marcel found live in Storybook").
3. **Availability states** — in-stock vs out-of-stock/unavailable, and exactly what changes per variation when unavailable (notify-me appearance, size-selector suppression, price behavior, mobile-specific differences).
4. **Image states** — single image vs multiple images (carousel arrows appear only for multi-image), hover-image-swap (which variation(s) get it), the touch slide-indicator (mobile/tablet only, mutually exclusive with arrows).
5. **Price states** — regular price, sale/was-now price, and which variation(s)/conditions show which, including the recent "was/now price" AC requirement that was added to `zimmProductCardContent` stories (search postbuild.md and plan.md for "was" and "now" and "sale").
6. **Size states** — normal size chips, disabled/unavailable size chips, "One size" (singular, non-interactive) state — and which variations show size chips at all.
7. **Badge states** — when a merchandiser badge shows, and the still-open "Dani Rivett carousel-suppression" gap (badge/hover-swap should be off for Homepage AND the Recently-Viewed carousel, but only Homepage got implemented) — get the exact quote and citation for this, it's an explicitly flagged known gap that any new stories should probably still reflect accurately (i.e. don't silently invent a 'recently-viewed' story variant that doesn't have a real code path).
8. **Any other explicitly-cited AC/Figma/comment requirement** for this component family you find in either file that doesn't fit the buckets above — list it separately rather than forcing a fit.
9. **Anything explicitly marked as an open question, known gap, deliberately out of scope, or "do not implement"** for this component — these should NOT be turned into new stories implying they're supported.

For each item, give: a short label, the concrete state/prop values involved, and the exact citation (quote + source: AC / Figma node ID / comment author+date / "Marcel, live Storybook"). Report as a structured list grouped by the buckets above, not prose narrative — I need this to be scannable and precise since I'll use it directly to decide which named-export stories to build.

const hoverRevealsSizeSelector = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && !isUnavailable;
const sizeSelectorUnavailable = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && Boolean(isUnavailable);
const bagHiddenOnMobile = config.hideBagOnMobile || (config.hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable && Boolean(isUnavailable));
const removeLabel = config.showRemove ? intl.formatMessage(messages.removeFromWishlist, { name }) : undefined;
const resolvedBadge = config.showBadge ? badge : undefined;
```

- **`isUnavailable`/notify-me wiring**: `showNotifyMe` requires *both* `isUnavailable` and a real `onNotifyMe` callback ("an organism that sets `isUnavailable` without a real callback should not show a dead notify-me button"). It's variation-agnostic — not restricted to `plp` at the type level or in this logic; any variation with both gets a notify-me button.
- **`sizeSelectorUnavailable`** is a *separate* derivation from `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` (not just its negation) — it permanently hides the size-chip wrapper (both hover states) when unavailable AND config says this variation normally reveals a size-selector on hover. It's also reused (per the docblock) to drive a mobile-only price→notify-me swap inside `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s recipe — no separate variable computed for that; the recipe just reads the same boolean for both purposes.
- **`bagHiddenOnMobile`** — combines `hideBagOnMobile` (PLP's unconditional mobile hide) OR'd with `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable && isUnavailable` (Wishlist's narrower conditional hide). This is the single boolean passed to the recipe as `hideBagOnMobile` in the `useMultiStyleConfig` call — the two source flags are collapsed before the recipe ever sees them.
- **`resolvedBadge`** — a straight gate, no priority/sort logic here (`badge` prop is already assumed to be the single already-resolved value; sorting a `c_productBadges` array is explicitly out of scope, owned by SFCC-225 upstream).
- **Carousel vs. single image**: **not decided in this file at all.** `images` is forwarded to `ZimmProductCardMedia` unconditionally, and `showControls` is passed as a bare boolean literal `true` unconditionally too — the molecule (`ZimmProductCardMedia`, out of scope for this file) owns whatever image-count-based carousel/single-image/arrows/indicator decision exists. This organism computes nothing about image count.
- **No `variation === ...` or `switch(variation)` branching anywhere in the file** — verified directly (`grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` → the only hit is the docblock line quoting that exact grep command; zero real hits). | `hoverHidesPrice` | local recomputed value (gated `&& !isUnavailable`) |

# Consolidate ZimmProductCard Storybook stories (delete `nodeCoverage/`, rebuild `index.stories.tsx`)

## Context

`ZimmProductCard` currently has two separate Storybook surfaces:
- `zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx` — title `Commerce/ZimmProductCard`, 8 curated stories organized by real product variant/state (variation × availability × image count).
- `zimmProductCard/nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx` — title `Commerce/ZimmProductCard/Coverage` (a nested sub-category), 12 stories organized strictly by Figma node ID (`{Home,PLP,Wishlist}_{Desktop,Mobile}_{Default,Unavailable}`), plus one explicit `Hero_ExcludedNotInScope` placeholder documenting an out-of-scope Figma node.

Marcel wants one consolidated collection instead: "a single collection of stories that are driven by the variants and states guided by the ACs, designs, and comments" — not by Figma node ID, and not split across two files/sidebar categories.

Two research passes plus one design pass (all independently re-verified against live source, not taken on trust) confirmed:
- `nodeCoverage/` is fully isolated — the only references to it anywhere in the repo are two self-referential JSDoc lines (each file mentioning the other's path). No test file, no Storybook config entry, nothing else depends on it. Deleting it is a clean, zero-blast-radius operation.
- `.storybook/main.js`'s `stories` glob is a recursive wildcard with no hardcoded per-folder paths — no config change needed.
- `index.test.tsx` (983 lines) has zero dependency on either story file's exports — confirmed by reading its import block directly.
- The CI `storybook-test` job (`@storybook/test-runner`, Playwright-based) only mounts stories and runs axe checks — no Chromatic/visual-snapshot step exists in this repo, so renaming/adding/removing exports carries no visual-baseline risk.
- The sibling molecules `zimmProductCardContent` and `zimmSizeChipGroup` already establish the target house style this codebase actually uses elsewhere: one file, many descriptive named exports, no separate coverage subfolder. `nodeCoverage/` is a one-off unique to this component, not the norm.
- Every one of the 12 `nodeCoverage` stories is a finer-grained (Desktop/Mobile × Default/Unavailable) decomposition of a state the main file's 8 stories already demonstrate via manual hover/resize — real content overlap, not distinct coverage.
- There are 3 confirmed real gaps in current coverage that the rebuild should close: Was/Now (sale) pricing, One Size, and price-loading — each a real, wired, AC/Figma-backed state with zero organism-level story today (though each already has precedent at the sibling `zimmProductCardContent`/`zimmSizeChipGroup` layer to model the naming/shape on).

Marcel confirmed (via AskUserQuestion) that this consolidation should **not** introduce a new `play` function — the file's existing "manual visual check only" pattern (documented in nearly every current story's own docblock, because Storybook's test runner can't reliably force real `:hover` CSS matching) stays as-is. The `MultipleImages` docblock just gets one added line noting the Fix H hover-out fix is part of that same manual check now.

## Approach

### 1. Delete `nodeCoverage/` entirely
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx` is the only file in that folder — delete the file and the now-empty folder. Nothing else to change (no config, no other source file references it).

### 2. Rewrite `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx`

**Keep all 8 existing stories, unchanged, in their current order** — each maps to a real, distinct, AC/Figma-backed state and none becomes redundant once the 3 new ones exist (confirmed explicitly — see "candidates considered and rejected" below):
`Default → PLPOutOfStock → Home → HomeOutOfStock → Wishlist → WishlistOutOfStock → SingleImage → MultipleImages`

Every existing per-story docblock (Fix D/E/F/G citations, the "live-verified real 375px viewport, 2026-09-04" evidence notes, the Wishlist "hover-reveals-size-selector is design-only, not AC-stated" caveat) carries forward **verbatim** — none of this is redundant or safe to drop; it's the only place several of these findings are recorded.

**One small addition to `MultipleImages`'s existing docblock** — append:
> Fix H (2026-09-05): hover-out now correctly hides the arrows again too (`:has(:focus-visible)`, not the old `:focus-within` which stuck open once a clicked arrow button kept real DOM focus) — part of the same manual hover check above, no `play` function added for it (see `index.tsx`'s own docblock point 6/Fix H for the full mechanism).

**Append 3 new stories** for the confirmed gaps, all extending `Default.args` (cheapest baseline that already has size chips wired; avoids Wishlist's extra required props for gaps that aren't about Wishlist):

```tsx
/**
 * Was/Now (sale) pricing (PRC-09): `originalPrice` set alongside `currentPrice` switches
 * ZimmProductCardContent → ZimmProductPrice to the "Was {X} Now {Y}" treatment (Figma node
 * 40001028:9179). Generic, variation-agnostic atom behaviour — the price atom has no
 * `variation` awareness at all — so demonstrated once here, off the same PLP baseline as
 * `Default`, not once per variation. Prices match zimmProductCardContent/index.stories.tsx's
 * own `WithSalePrice` exactly, so the two layers read as the same fixture product.
 */
export const WithSalePrice: Story = {
  args: {
    ...Default.args,
    currentPrice: '$416.50',
    originalPrice: '$595.00',
  },
  render: (args) => <LiveSizeSelectionCard {...args} />,
};

/**
 * One size offered: ZimmSizeChipGroup's `values.length === 1` branch renders a single
 * non-interactive `<span>` (Figma node 40003066:34866), not a one-item radiogroup — see that
 * component's own `OneSize` story and zimmProductCardContent's own `WithSizeChipsOneSize` for
 * the same branch at the other two composed layers. Plain args, NOT wrapped in
 * `LiveSizeSelectionCard`: there is nothing to select in this branch (it never reaches the
 * chip-click/keyboard-navigation code path at all), so the interactive wrapper would
 * misleadingly imply a selection state that cannot exist here — same reasoning
 * `WithSizeChipsOneSize` documents for itself.
 */
export const OneSize: Story = {
  args: {
    ...Default.args,
    sizeChipValues: [{ value: 'os', label: 'One size' }],
  },
};

/**
 * A variant re-fetch in progress: `isPriceLoading` forwards straight through to
 * ZimmProductCardContent → ZimmProductPrice, which renders its own invisible placeholder,
 * preserving the price's layout slot rather than collapsing it. See that atom's own docblock
 * and zimmProductCardContent's own `LoadingPrice` story for the mechanism.
 */
export const LoadingPrice: Story = {
  args: {
    ...Default.args,
    currentPrice: undefined,
    isPriceLoading: true,
  },
  render: (args) => <LiveSizeSelectionCard {...args} />,
};
```

No new imports needed — `PRIMARY_IMAGE`/`HOVER_IMAGE`/`SIZES`/`ZimmSizeChipValue` and `LiveSizeSelectionCard` are all already defined in the current file and reused as-is.

**Candidates considered and rejected** (for the record, so a future reader knows these were deliberately left out, not missed):
- A Wishlist "attributes One Size" story (`size: 'One size'` as plain text) — this is `ZimmProductCardContent`'s `showAttributes` text line, a pure passthrough with zero organism-level logic on top, already fully proven at that molecule's own layer (`WithAttributesOneSize`). Adding it here would be exactly the "story per sub-section" duplication `.claude/rules/components.md` warns against.
- A Recently-Viewed-rail or Hero placeholder story — neither has a real code path (no such `variation` union member exists); a story would misrepresent the component as supporting them.
- Combining the 3 new gap axes with each other or with availability (e.g. "OneSize + OutOfStock") — would be exactly the combinatorial "every possible prop combination" expansion `.claude/rules/components.md` prohibits.

**Module (top-of-file) docblock** — replace the current "18-node coverage matrix" bookkeeping (moot once `nodeCoverage/` no longer exists to justify the split) with:
- Keep verbatim: the "mobile behaviour is a real `@media (min-width: 48em)` viewport query, not a container query... live-verified in a real browser at a genuine 375px viewport" paragraph — still true, still practically useful.
- Add this Hero-orphan note (condensed from `nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx`'s own investigation, its only current home):
  ```
   * Hero (Figma nodes 40004599:89265, 40004638:120484) is out of scope, not merely uncovered:
   * confirmed orphaned design node with no owning ticket anywhere in Jira — SFCC-81, SFCC-218
   * and SFCC-882 were each read directly and all three describe a full-width page-level PLP
   * banner that shares the word "Hero" by coincidence, not this card.
   * `ZimmProductCardProps['variation']` has no fourth value to render it with, so there is no
   * story for it here — a placeholder story rendering no real component would misrepresent this
   * file's own "every story is a real, supported state" contract.
  ```
- Add one line pointing at `index.tsx`'s own module docblock as the canonical source for the full Fix A–H narrative, so per-story docblocks here stay focused on "what this story proves."

**`LiveSizeSelectionCard`'s docblock** — trim the now-dangling sentence "moved here so every enabled-size-chip story across both `zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx` and `zimmProductCard/nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx` can share one implementation instead of each retyping it" to describe it as this file's own helper only. Implementation itself is unchanged.

**Execution note**: `index.stories.tsx` currently has an uncommitted placeholder-SVG-fill-colour change sitting in the working tree from earlier this session (already-correct `#f6f4f1`/`#f9f8f6`/`#f2e9e0` values, visible in the file as read). This rewrite carries those values forward as part of the same fixture constants — no separate handling needed, it's naturally subsumed into this change.

## Files touched

- **Delete**: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx` (and the resulting empty `nodeCoverage/` folder)
- **Rewrite**: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx`

No other file needs to change — confirmed via direct source reads: `.storybook/main.js` (glob-based, no per-folder entries), `.storybook/preview.tsx` / `.storybook/a11yExcludes.ts` (no title-keyed references to either file), `index.test.tsx` (no import of either story file), `.github/workflows/qa.yml` (change-detection filter already covers `overrides/app/components/**`, no new filter needed).

## Verification

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` — must stay clean.
2. `npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/` — confirm `index.test.tsx` (which has zero dependency on story exports) stays green.
3. `npm run lint` — confirm no new errors beyond the existing pre-existing baseline (5 errors, all in unrelated `product-detail` files).
4. `npm run audit:tokens` — confirm no new raw-value findings introduced.
5. Ask the developer to restart Storybook (per AGENTS.md, don't run dev servers directly) and manually confirm:
   - Sidebar shows exactly one `Commerce/ZimmProductCard` entry with 11 stories — no `Coverage` sub-entry.
   - `WithSalePrice` renders "Was $595.00 Now $416.50".
   - `OneSize` renders a single non-interactive, bordered "One size" label (not a radiogroup).
   - `LoadingPrice` renders the price atom's loading placeholder instead of a price.
   - `MultipleImages`: hovering still reveals the arrows; moving the mouse away now correctly hides them again (Fix H) instead of staying stuck open.
6. `git status` should show exactly the `nodeCoverage/` deletion and the `index.stories.tsx` rewrite — nothing else touched.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNPreBuild

The gate before code. Nothing gets built until every source has been checked and every gap has
been named.

**Intended model: Opus 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — set it
yourself before invoking. The plan synthesis step delegates to the `zm-planner` agent, which is
pinned to Opus regardless of the session model, so the expensive judgement runs on Opus either
way.

**Input:** `SFCC-83 and 84 together` — a Jira key (e.g. `SFCC-194`), optionally followed by a depth.
If no key is given, ask for one before doing anything else.

## Depth

Depth is a parameter, not an adverb. Pick one and say which you are using:

| Depth | Jira + Confluence | Codebase | Figma |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quick` | the ticket and its direct links | branch state, file tiers | the named node only |
| `standard` *(default)* | ticket, links, comments; targeted Confluence search | tiers, blast radius, nearest existing pattern | node, variants, states |
| `exhaustive` | full link graph, all comments, related epics, all matching Confluence | above, plus every consumer of every touched file and the exemplar PR diffs | node, all variants, all states, all viewports, token mapping |

Never substitute a stronger adverb for a depth. "In-depth full-on exhaustive" is not a level;
`exhaustive` is.

---

## Phase 0 — position

Call `/session-start`. It confirms the branch, reads the tracking docs, runs health checks and
states current position.

Then confirm one thing it does not: **you cannot be on `develop` or `main`.** A `PreToolUse` hook
blocks every Write and Edit on those branches, so a plan handed to the builder from `develop` is
dead on arrival. If the branch is wrong, say so and stop — do not create a branch unasked.

---

## Phase 1 — gather

Run these **in parallel**. Each one ends in its own findings block. Never let a clean source hide
a broken one — report all five, even when four are fine.

### Jira — `mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue`

Pull the story and read all of it: description, requirements, acceptance criteria, linked design,
attachments, linked work items, and the full comment thread. Comments routinely carry the
decision that contradicts the description.

Flag: missing or untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments ·
no linked design · attachments referenced in prose but not attached · linked work items that are
still open and block this one · a decision made in comments that never made it into the description.

### Confluence — `confluence_search`, `confluence_get_page`

Search for anything bearing on this story: TSDs, integration docs, data dictionaries, decisions.

Flag: no TSD where the work clearly needs one · a TSD that contradicts the ticket · documentation
describing an approach the codebase does not implement · a page last updated before a decision
that supersedes it.

### FED handbook — `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md`

The build approach: tokens, components, CSS structure, overriding, accessibility, tests, stories.
Part I is the machine, Part II the procedure, Part III the role.

Flag: handbook guidance that contradicts what the codebase now does · a claim whose cited
`file:line` no longer resolves · anything the story needs that the handbook does not cover.

The handbook is a derived account, not the source. **Where it disagrees with
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, that file wins** — and say so, because it means the handbook
is stale.

### Codebase

Branch state, and the shape of what is about to be touched.

- Confirm `develop` is current with `origin/develop`.
- For every likely-touched file: tier and owner, from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and
  `protectedFiles.md`. **Never from `.claude/registry/*.md`** — its Tier column is a derived
  heuristic and is wrong in places.
- Call `/audit-tier <path>` for anything you are unsure about. It also returns import blast radius.
- Find the nearest existing pattern. This codebase has strong precedent; matching it is cheaper
  and more reviewable than inventing.
- Read the exemplar PRs when the story touches their surface: **PR #64** (ui-kit atom/molecule,
  four-file pattern, co-located recipe, render-slot wiring), **PR #59** (global-chrome component,
  co-located recipe with shared cross-file values), **PR #56** (pure token layer, no component
  change).

Flag: any Tier 1 file in the likely set · high blast radius (a shared file with many consumers) ·
work that crosses squad territory · an existing pattern the story would contradict.

### Figma

- Design System 2026 — `https://www.figma.com/design/wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/Zimmermann_Design_System_2026`
- Zimmermann_Designs — `https://www.figma.com/design/QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs/Zimmermann_Designs`

**Ask for one node URL per variant and per state**, not one per component. If the file-level
links are not enough to resolve the specific component, stop and ask Marcel. Do not guess at
which node the story means, and do not build from a neighbouring node that looks close.

Check:

- **Completeness** — every variant and every state: hover, focus, active, disabled, loading,
  error, empty, success.
- **Currency** — is this design archived or superseded? Triage archived against current before
  anyone builds to it. An archived node that still renders is a trap.
- **Tokenisation** — does every value map to an existing `--zimm-*` token, or is a new token
  being introduced? A new token is Tier 1 and needs the designer.
- **Responsiveness** — frames exist at 402 / 1023 / 1440; breakpoint tokens are 768 / 860 / 1024.
  **The 768–1022 band is unframed**, so anything in it is an inference, not a design.

Two measurement traps that have produced false defects here. Flag a comparison that hits either:

- **Node type decides comparability.** Figma TEXT nodes report a cap-height box, which is not
  comparable to a CSS line box — never file a mismatch from one. FRAMES and INSTANCES report a
  real box and are directly comparable.
- **The two Figma files must never be cross-compared.** The Design System file and the Designs
  file are different sources; a delta between them is not a defect.

**No design is a blocker, not licence to invent.** If the ACs name something Figma does not have,
that is a finding for Marcel — or an explicit **provisional**, labelled as such and carried into
the plan as an assumption. Never fill the gap silently.

Flag: missing variants or states · a design that is archived or superseded · values with no token
· the unframed tablet band left to inference · a design that contradicts an established component
· no design at all where the story implies one.

---

## Phase 2 — reuse

These already exist. Call them; do not reimplement them.

1. `/feature-spec` — turns the gathered picture into a scoped implementation plan and emits a
   ready-to-paste scoped prompt.
2. `/scope-check` — run it **on that prompt**. It verdicts SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED and rewrites
   risky prompts. This is the highest-leverage gate available; do not skip it.
3. `/audit-tier <path>` — per file, wherever scope-check flags something specific.

Two known traps when calling these:

- `/code-quality` defaults to diffing against **`main`**; `/pr-checklist` diffs against
  **`develop`**. On a feature branch these give different file sets. Always pass explicit scope.
- `/pr-checklist` already calls `/code-quality` internally. Calling both doubles the audit.

None of these skills emits machine-readable output — they all return prose for a human. If you
need to branch on a result, restate the verdict yourself rather than parsing theirs.

---

## Phase 3 — the gate

This is the part that earns the skill. Produce one table, every source, every gap:

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Severity is one of:

- 🔴 **BLOCKED** — cannot plan around it. A missing AC, an absent design, a Tier 1 file with no
  owner approval, a `scope-check` BLOCKED verdict. **Stop here.** Report and wait for Marcel.
- 🟡 **CLARIFY** — plannable, but the plan carries a stated assumption. Name the assumption
  explicitly in the plan so it is visible if it turns out wrong.
- 🔵 **NOTE** — worth knowing, does not affect the plan.

**Do not fill a gap with an assumption and carry on silently.** A missing acceptance criterion is
a finding, not something to infer. The whole point of the gate is that it stops.

---

## Phase 4 — plan

Delegate to the `zm-planner` agent (Opus). Give it everything gathered — all five findings blocks,
the `/feature-spec` output, and the `/scope-check` verdict.

It returns: goal statement · scale call (multi-commit or multi-branch, with reasoning) · file
manifest with tiers and owners · steps with concrete pass criteria · per-step loop configuration ·
open questions.

Write the result to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`, and write the Phase 3 gate
table to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/findings.md`.

Create the run directory if it does not exist. **Never write run state into the repo.**

---

## Phase 5 — handoff

Present to Marcel, in **"ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead"** register — not dumbed down, but without
jargon that gets in the way. Lead with the consequence, then the mechanism, then the fix.

1. The gate table — blockers first.
2. The plan summary — scale call, step count, file count with tier breakdown.
3. Every stated assumption, gathered in one place.
4. The paths to `plan.md` and `findings.md`.

Then say plainly whether this is ready for `zimmerMANNBuild`, or what is blocking it.

**Put decisions to him one at a time, using AskUserQuestion.** Do not present a wall of choices
and do not bundle unrelated calls into one question.

**This skill stops here. It never invokes `zimmerMANNBuild`** — Marcel does, once he has read the
gate. Discover → report → wait for approval → and execution is a separate, deliberate act.

**Do not hand off with an unresolved 🔴.** Handing a blocked plan to the builder is how a
build burns an afternoon on the wrong thing.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never modify anything.** This skill reads, checks and plans. The only files it writes are
  under `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/`. No repo file is touched — not one.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `zimmermann-pwa/.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
  `CODEOWNERS`, `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. All Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never infer squad ownership** from `squadA.md` / `squadB.md`. They contradict each other on
  PDP/PLP and are both drafts. Read `CODEOWNERS`.
- **Never present a gap as resolved because it seems minor.** Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Say what you did not check.** A source you skipped is itself a finding.
- **Provenance, not proximity.** A document living in the codebase is a downstream artifact, not
  a source. If you cannot locate the original source for a claim, flag it **provenance unknown**
  and ask. Never fabricate a source, and never fall back to citing a codebase path as one.
- **Local-only docs are never citable.** `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` and its predecessors are
  Marcel's personal files. **They must never appear in a PR, a commit message, or a code
  comment.** Where the same rule exists in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`, cite the repo file
  instead — that is the citable source.
- **Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full treatment. At `quick` depth,
  drop the exemplar-PR read and the blast-radius sweep, and keep the gate. Nothing too crazy,
  no overthinking.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/session-start

Run the mandatory session start ritual defined in [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). Do this before writing any code.

## Steps (in order — do not skip any)

1. **Confirm branch** — run `git branch --show-current`. If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — no edits permitted (see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 1). If it matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`, read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) in full before proceeding — the supervised-edit and back-merge rules there apply on top of the Hard Rules.

2. **Read tracking docs** — read these in parallel:
   - [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md) — current phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending
   - [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](../../../.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) — what exists this sprint, what is deferred. **Read before scoping any new work.**
   - [.docs/memory/feedback.md](../../../.docs/memory/feedback.md) — patterns to avoid or repeat
   - [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md) — current `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version and review state
   - [../session-notes.md](../session-notes.md) — lightweight, **gitignored, per-developer** carryover notes from your last local session (a Claude-writable staging area — see "Living Memory" below for how this differs from `.docs/memory/`). If it has pending items, surface them in step 4's "blockers or outstanding issues" and clear/promote each once resolved. It won't exist for a fresh clone or a teammate who hasn't used it — that's expected, skip silently.

3. **Health checks** — run when the helper exists:
   - `bash scripts/healthCheckAll.sh` — If the script does not exist yet, state that clearly and skip.

4. **State current position** — in plain language, say exactly:
   - Current branch
   - Current sprint / phase (from `projectState.md`)
   - The last completed task and the next task
   - Any blockers or outstanding issues

   Format: "Resuming from: [last completed task]. Next: [next task]. [Any blockers or health issues]."

5. **Confirm readiness** — ask if the user wants to proceed with the stated next task or redirect to something else.

Do not write any code until this ritual is complete and the user has confirmed direction.

---

## Living Memory — what belongs where

`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Keep it current — update the relevant file whenever a session produces new information that belongs there.

**`.claude/session-notes.md` is different: a lightweight, Claude-writable, gitignored, per-developer staging area** (same pattern as `userProfile.md` below, but for tasks rather than profile info) for short-lived carryover items (e.g. "still need to do X next session") that haven't been promoted to `.docs/memory/` yet. It's **not** shared via git — each developer's notes stay local, so they never conflict or overwrite a teammate's. Unlike the files below, Claude may write to it directly. Use it for quick pending-item tracking; move anything durable and team-relevant into the right `.docs/memory/` file once it's confirmed, and clear the note.

| File | What belongs there | When to update |
|---|---|---|
| `architecture.md` | Stack decisions, overrides pattern, key paths, structural choices | A new integration is added, a structural decision is made, or a key path changes |
| `projectState.md` | Phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending, unresolved dependencies | Any integration goes live, a phase changes, a feature is completed, or a dependency is resolved |
| `feedback.md` | What worked, what failed, patterns to avoid or repeat | After discovering a gotcha, a failed approach, or a validated pattern |
| `references.md` | Service URLs, API keys, credentials, logins, dashboards | A new credential or service URL is introduced (system roles live in `architecture.md`) |
| `userProfile.md` | User's role, expertise, working style, preferences | User shares a preference or working-style detail that should persist |

**Rules:**
- Never leave a file with only its placeholder comment — populate it the moment you learn something that belongs there.
- **No duplication.** Every fact has exactly one home. Before writing something, check whether it already lives in another doc — if it does, reference that doc instead of copying. Applies across all `.md` files: `AGENTS.md`, memory files, and PRDs.
- **Conciseness.** Keep all `.md` instructions concise.

  (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.
