1	*This document is for documenting what has been learned - What worked, what failed, what NOT to do again.*
2	
3	## SFCC-751 QA automation pipeline (2026-08-24/25)
4	
5	- **Test locally before pushing anything that triggers real CI, especially BrowserStack** — it
6	  costs real session quota. When debugging a CI failure, reproduce it locally first rather than
7	  keep iterating against a live PR. Confirmed developer preference — redirected mid-session after
8	  a live-PR debugging detour: "I wanted to test this via the CLI BEFORE we push to Git and it
9	  runs its tests."
10	- **`browserstack-node-sdk` requires its config file literally named `browserstack.yml`, no
11	  leading dot.** A `.browserstack.yml` is silently never found — every SDK-driven run fails at
12	  config resolution before any test executes. This repo had the dotted name since it was first
13	  created and never caught it, because no PR had ever gotten `e2e-browserstack` far enough to hit
14	  that step successfully before SFCC-751's first real run (PR #61).
15	- **BrowserStack Test Observability groups results by test *title* across Playwright projects,
16	  not by project.** Two tests sharing an identical title (the same `test()` running under both
17	  `chromium` and `mobile-chrome`) collapse to one dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded*
18	  status — confirmed via the real API, not just the dashboard UI (a build with 11 real chromium
19	  passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles reported `passed: 0,
20	  skipped: 11`). `test.skip()` does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and
21	  still clobbers. Real fix: genuinely separate spec files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/`
22	  folders, which `playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already routes
23	  correctly (`chromium` ignores `**/mobile/**`, `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`) — not a
24	  same-file/distinct-title workaround, which still gets the "wrong" project's test collected (and
25	  skipped) regardless of its title.
26	- **Jira Cloud's "Sprint" field has no stable API alias.** It's `customfield_10020` on this
27	  instance specifically (confirmed live via a real field search) — an instance-specific ID, not
28	  safe to assume unchanged on a different Jira site.
29	- **BrowserStack's Test Observability API strips the leading `@` from Playwright tags.** A spec's
30	  own `@zephyr:KEY` tag comes back as `zephyr:KEY` (no `@`) in the `Get Tests` API response —
31	  easy to get wrong since the source `.spec.js` file's tags do have `@`.
32	- **Chakra modal close animations aren't instant.** A consent-dismiss helper that clicks decline
33	  and returns immediately can hand control back while the dialog is still mid-fade-out and
34	  technically "visible" — a caller that immediately checks for a *different* dialog right after
35	  can match both and get a Playwright strict-mode "resolved to 2 elements" error. Wait for
36	  `state: 'hidden'` after the click, not just for the click to register.
37

*This document is for documenting what has been learned - What worked, what failed, what NOT to do again.*

## SFCC-751 QA automation pipeline (2026-08-24/25)

- **Test locally before pushing anything that triggers real CI, especially BrowserStack** — it
  costs real session quota. When debugging a CI failure, reproduce it locally first rather than
  keep iterating against a live PR. Confirmed developer preference — redirected mid-session after
  a live-PR debugging detour: "I wanted to test this via the CLI BEFORE we push to Git and it
  runs its tests."
- **`browserstack-node-sdk` requires its config file literally named `browserstack.yml`, no
  leading dot.** A `.browserstack.yml` is silently never found — every SDK-driven run fails at
  config resolution before any test executes. This repo had the dotted name since it was first
  created and never caught it, because no PR had ever gotten `e2e-browserstack` far enough to hit
  that step successfully before SFCC-751's first real run (PR #61).
- **BrowserStack Test Observability groups results by test *title* across Playwright projects,
  not by project.** Two tests sharing an identical title (the same `test()` running under both
  `chromium` and `mobile-chrome`) collapse to one dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded*
  status — confirmed via the real API, not just the dashboard UI (a build with 11 real chromium
  passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles reported `passed: 0,
  skipped: 11`). `test.skip()` does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and
  still clobbers. Real fix: genuinely separate spec files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/`
  folders, which `playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already routes
  correctly (`chromium` ignores `**/mobile/**`, `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`) — not a
  same-file/distinct-title workaround, which still gets the "wrong" project's test collected (and
  skipped) regardless of its title.
- **Jira Cloud's "Sprint" field has no stable API alias.** It's `customfield_10020` on this
  instance specifically (confirmed live via a real field search) — an instance-specific ID, not
  safe to assume unchanged on a different Jira site.
- **BrowserStack's Test Observability API strips the leading `@` from Playwright tags.** A spec's
  own `@zephyr:KEY` tag comes back as `zephyr:KEY` (no `@`) in the `Get Tests` API response —
  easy to get wrong since the source `.spec.js` file's tags do have `@`.
- **Chakra modal close animations aren't instant.** A consent-dismiss helper that clicks decline
  and returns immediately can hand control back while the dialog is still mid-fade-out and
  technically "visible" — a caller that immediately checks for a *different* dialog right after
  can match both and get a Playwright strict-mode "resolved to 2 elements" error. Wait for
  `state: 'hidden'` after the click, not just for the click to register.

  "summary": "Read More SEO Text Block & Conditional Background",
  "description": "**As a** Shopper,

**I want** to see contextual page information next to the breadcrumb navigation,

**so that** I can understand where I am on the site and discover relevant content.

----

**Context:**

This story covers two related UI behaviours tied to the area next to the breadcrumb navigation at the bottom of the page (below Recently Viewed).

**SEO text block:** A set of labelled accordion sections is displayed beneath the Recently Viewed component. The sections are collapsed by default, showing only the section header. Each section can be individually expanded to reveal its SEO copy — for example, category descriptions or editorial content — and collapsed again by clicking the header. The section headings and body copy are CMS-managed in Contentful and are page-contextual; the content rendered depends on the page the shopper is on. This content is independent of the Recently Viewed component itself and is always present on the page regardless of whether Recently Viewed is rendered.

**Conditional background colour:** The Recently Viewed component has its own background colour. When the component is not rendered — for example, when the shopper has no browsing history — the SEO text block would otherwise appear against an orphaned coloured band that doesn't match the white content above it. The background colour of this section must therefore adapt: when Recently Viewed is rendered, it uses the standard component background; when Recently Viewed is not rendered, the background blends with the white section above to avoid a visual break.



Current (needs redesign):

564	### 7. Building against absent data
565	
566	#### Three patterns, only the first correct
567	
568	**Guard, then render inert but perceivable.** Never render nothing where a control was
569	promised; never render a control that can't act.
570	
571	- **An empty-string fallback is a layout bug** — `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that
572	  **keeps its margins**, measured as a roughly 64px void. It doesn't collapse; it reserves
573	  space for nothing.
574	- **A silent element swap actively lies** — it promises an affordance that isn't there.
575	- **Fix at the atom**, not at each call site.
576	
577	#### The three-tier policy — the most reusable decision in the footer build
578	
579	Behaviour differs by what the content *is*:
580	
581	| Content class | Behaviour | Why |
582	|---|---|---|
583	| **Structural** (`footerConfig`) | render **nothing** — `if (!footerData) return null` | no fallback to placeholder once wired to live data, so an outage doesn't ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers |
584	| **Microcopy** (`uiCopy`) | fall back to the **English literal** | losing a button label to an outage should never blank a control |
585	| **Per-item destination** (a contact href) | degrade **that item only** to a labelled non-interactive `<span>` | perceivable, but no false affordance |
586	
587	The per-item case is the carefully argued one: no `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing promises an
588	action that cannot be performed (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4) — but **labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so
589	a screen-reader user learns the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoiding the 1.1.1
590	information loss an earlier `aria-hidden` caused).
591	
592	The same treatment is reused three times for "control with no action": the contact fallback,
593	`ZimmNavItem`'s no-href branch (renders a `<button>` that doesn't navigate), and `BottomBar`'s
594	locale placeholder (a `<div>`, deliberately not a `<button>`).
595	
596	#### Never branch on localised CMS text
597	
598	`footerNavGroup` carries `showContactChannels: boolean` rather than matching
599	`heading === 'Contact'` — because `heading` is localised and silently stops matching the moment
600	an editor writes "Kontakt" or "Contacto". This footer ships to eight storefronts.
601	
602	#### Guarding hrefs
603	
604	Every CMS-sourced href passes `isSafeHref` before reaching an anchor. The subtlety: WHATWG URL
605	parsing strips C0 control characters, tab, LF and CR *before* scheme detection, so a naive
606	`^javascript:` regex is bypassed by `java\tscript:`. **Normalise, then test.**
607	
608	---
609

611	
612	New section. The footer rendered correctly in dev and was blank on the test tier, and nothing
613	in the component was wrong.

### 7. Building against absent data

#### Three patterns, only the first correct

**Guard, then render inert but perceivable.** Never render nothing where a control was
promised; never render a control that can't act.

- **An empty-string fallback is a layout bug** — `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that
  **keeps its margins**, measured as a roughly 64px void. It doesn't collapse; it reserves
  space for nothing.
- **A silent element swap actively lies** — it promises an affordance that isn't there.
- **Fix at the atom**, not at each call site.

#### The three-tier policy — the most reusable decision in the footer build

Behaviour differs by what the content *is*:

| Content class | Behaviour | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Structural** (`footerConfig`) | render **nothing** — `if (!footerData) return null` | no fallback to placeholder once wired to live data, so an outage doesn't ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers |
| **Microcopy** (`uiCopy`) | fall back to the **English literal** | losing a button label to an outage should never blank a control |
| **Per-item destination** (a contact href) | degrade **that item only** to a labelled non-interactive `<span>` | perceivable, but no false affordance |

The per-item case is the carefully argued one: no `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing promises an
action that cannot be performed (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4) — but **labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so
a screen-reader user learns the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoiding the 1.1.1
information loss an earlier `aria-hidden` caused).

The same treatment is reused three times for "control with no action": the contact fallback,
`ZimmNavItem`'s no-href branch (renders a `<button>` that doesn't navigate), and `BottomBar`'s
locale placeholder (a `<div>`, deliberately not a `<button>`).

#### Never branch on localised CMS text

`footerNavGroup` carries `showContactChannels: boolean` rather than matching
`heading === 'Contact'` — because `heading` is localised and silently stops matching the moment
an editor writes "Kontakt" or "Contacto". This footer ships to eight storefronts.

#### Guarding hrefs

Every CMS-sourced href passes `isSafeHref` before reaching an anchor. The subtlety: WHATWG URL
parsing strips C0 control characters, tab, LF and CR *before* scheme detection, so a naive
`^javascript:` regex is bypassed by `java\tscript:`. **Normalise, then test.**

---

### 8. CMS data and the tier reality

New section. The footer rendered correctly in dev and was blank on the test tier, and nothing
in the component was wrong.

### Play 1 — The reuse & dependency check

Four rungs: use as-is → override → compose existing atoms → build new. Rung 4 is rarest and
needs justification.

**Where to look:** `.claude/registry/` for `Origin` (`Custom` / `Override` / **`Base`**), then
`ui-kits/`. ⚠️ The registry's `Tier` column is unreliable — `generateRegistry.mjs:133-215`
hardcodes tiers, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything to Tier 4.

**`Origin = Base` is the hidden cost.** It means copy-first: mirror the file, convert to TS,
verify the override renders, *then* build. That's real effort and it belongs in the estimate.
Eight components referenced throughout `.claude/rules/` are still base.

**The `shared/ui` barrel exception.** Overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` to propagate styling into
base cart/checkout/account looks like enormous leverage. It intercepts nothing — the barrel
re-exports relatively, which the resolver doesn't rewrite, and 212 base files import the barrel
(195 excluding tests) while **0** import the individual module. Don't scope a story around it.

**Duplicate atoms are a human problem.** No tool detects "this is a second Button." The fix
that makes it self-service is one line in the BA's story template: *name the component, and
state whether it exists.*

#### The atoms governance model — decided

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/
```

Tier by composition (what the component's own template renders), camelCase for
Zimmermann-authored, a registered recipe always.

⚠️ **The rules set is split on this.** `components.md` and `conventions.md` contain **zero**
occurrences of `ui-kits`, `atoms`, `molecules` or `organisms`. `new-component/SKILL.md:29`
still scaffolds to the flat path. `.docs/architecture.md` contradicts itself. Reconciling this
is a standing item.

---

### Play 2 — Estimation validation

**The re-baseline to say once:** pages go *down*, components go *up by more*. Component-based
decomposition front-loads the work.

Split component-build effort from page-composition effort in every estimate. They have
different risk profiles and different owners.

# Audit: SFCC-83 (Recently Viewed rail) + SFCC-84 (Full History page)

## 1. Existing carousel / rail / horizontal-scroll infrastructure

**No product-rail or horizontal-list component exists anywhere in `overrides/`.** Not in `ui-kits/`, not elsewhere. Verified by grep for `carousel|slider|scroller|swiper` across all `.ts`/`.tsx` in `overrides/app` — every hit is one of three unrelated things:

**(a) A per-card image pager inside `ZimmProductCardMedia`** — this is intra-card image paging, not a multi-product rail:
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx:156` — `const [currentIndex, setCurrentIndex] = useState(0);`
- `:298` / `:306` — `onClick={() => goToRelativeSlide(-1)}` / `(1)`
- `:293` — `<chakra.div __css={styles.carousel} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.carousel}>` (the prev/next arrows wrapper)
- `:315` — `<ZimmSlideIndicator count={totalSlides} activeIndex={currentIndex} />`
- Files: `index.tsx`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`, `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` (all four present; **no** `.css.test.ts`)

**(b) `ZimmSlideIndicator` molecule** — a read-only segmented position indicator, touch-only, at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/`. Its docblock (`index.tsx:22-32`) states it is for "the PDP/card image strip", renders nothing for `count <= 1`, and is "Touch-only per the resolved arrows-vs-indicator split (SFCC-236)". Files: `index.tsx`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`, `zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts`, `zimmSlideIndicator.css.test.ts` (five files — has a dedicated recipe test).

**(c) `carousel` / `carousel-selected` icon names** in `zimmIcon` and `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx:47` (`CarouselIcon`) / `:64` (`CarouselSelectedIcon`) — icon assets only.

### Base `@salesforce/retail-react-app` components

Both exist in node_modules and **neither is overridden**:

| Path | Exists | Overridden in `overrides/`? |
|---|---|---|
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller/index.jsx` (8275 B) + `index.test.js` (4191 B) | Yes | **No** — `overrides/app/components/product-scroller` does not exist |
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products/index.jsx` (8526 B, no test) | Yes | **No** — `overrides/app/components/recommended-products` does not exist |

Neither base component has a `.css.ts` recipe or a Storybook story (they are plain upstream JSX with inline Chakra props).

`product-scroller/index.jsx` is a `forwardRef` horizontal scroller: "Renders a scrollable, horizontal container of products with native scroll snapping and manual button controls" (`:22-23`). Props: `header, title, products, isLoading, scrollProps, itemWidth = {base: '70%', md: '40%', lg: 'calc(25% - 15px)'}, productTileProps` (`:28-38`). It scrolls by `scrollRef.current?.scrollBy({left: direction * offsetWidth, behavior: 'smooth'})` (`:47-53`), returns `null` when not loading and no products (`:41-43`), and renders base `ProductTile` (`:17`) — **not** `ZimmProductCard`.

`recommended-products/index.jsx` wraps `ProductScroller` (`:12`, `:190`) and calls `useEinstein()` (`:13`, `:40-41`), fetching by `zone` or `recommender` (`:68-78`) and firing `sendViewReco` (`:96`) + `dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations` (`:103`).

**Both base components are already consumed by override pages:**
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:17` imports `ProductScroller`; used at `:100` — `<ProductScroller products={productSearchResult?.hits} isLoading={productsLoading} />`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:54` imports `RecommendedProducts`; rendered three times at `:1108`, `:1123`, `:1138`

Note: `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts:71` contains a comment referencing "the base SFCC product-scroller's own `scrollProps.sx`" — the base scroller's scrollbar-hiding CSS was used as precedent, but no code was shared.

---

## 2. `ZimmProductCard` contract

File: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` (475 lines).

### Variation union — exactly three members

`ZimmProductCardVariation` (`:227-230`) = `'plp' | 'home' | 'wishlist'`, derived from the three variation types. The exported props union is `ZimmProductCardProps` (`:224-225`):

```
export type ZimmProductCardProps = ZimmProductCardBaseProps &
  (ZimmProductCardPlpVariation | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation);
```

**There is no `recentlyViewed` / rail variation member.**

### Base props — `ZimmProductCardBaseProps` (`:158-188`), shared by all three

| Prop | Type | Req? | Line |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | **required** | `:163` |
| `href` | `string` | **required** | `:166` |
| `name` | `string` | **required** | `:167` |
| `headingLevel` | `'h1' \| 'h2' \| 'h3'` (via `ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductCardContent>['headingLevel']`, `:145`) | **required** | `:168` |
| `primaryImage` | `ZimmProductCardImage` (= `ZimmProductCardMediaImage`, `:140`) | **required** | `:169` |
| `hoverImage` | `ZimmProductCardImage` | optional | `:170` |
| `images` | `ZimmProductCardImage[]` | optional | `:171` |
| `currentPrice` | `string` | optional | `:172` |
| `originalPrice` | `string` | optional | `:173` |
| `isPriceLoading` | `boolean` | optional | `:174` |
| `isUnavailable` | `boolean` | optional | `:175` |
| `onNotifyMe` | `() => void` | optional | `:178` |
| `badge` | `string` | optional | `:187` |

### Per-variation additions

**`ZimmProductCardPlpVariation` (`:190-196`)**
- `variation: 'plp'` (required discriminant)
- `onAddToBag?: () => void`
- `sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[]`
- `selectedSizeChipValue?: string`
- `onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void`

**`ZimmProductCardHomeVariation` (`:198-201`)**
- `variation: 'home'` — and nothing else. Comment `:200`: "No additions — Home never shows the bag, attributes, or size chips (see VARIATION_CONFIG)."

**`ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation` (`:203-222`)**
- `variation: 'wishlist'`
- `colour: string` — **required** (`:206`)
- `size: string` — **required** (`:207`)
- `onRemove: () => void` — **required** (`:209`, "a wishlist card with no way to remove itself is a spec violation")
- `onAddToBag?: () => void` (`:211`)
- `sizeChipValues?`, `selectedSizeChipValue?`, `onSizeChipSelect?` (`:219-221`)

Also exported: `ZimmProductCardImage` (`:140`), `ZimmProductCardBaseProps` (`:158`), and all three variation types.

### Complete `VARIATION_CONFIG` table (`:290-330`) — 11 flags × 3 variations

| Flag | `home` | `plp` | `wishlist` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `showBag` | `false` | `true` | `true` |
| `showAttributes` | `false` | `false` | `true` |
| `showSizeChips` | `false` | `true` | `true` |
| `hoverHidesPrice` | `false` | `true` | `true` |
| `hoverRevealsPrice` | **`true`** | `false` | `false` |
| `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` | `false` | `true` | `true` |
| `showRemove` | `false` | `false` | `true` |
| `hideBagOnMobile` | `false` | **`true`** | `false` |
| `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable` | `false` | `false` | **`true`** |
| `showBadge` | `false` | `true` | `true` |
| `showHoverImageSwap` | `false` | `true` | `true` |

Flag type declared at `:248-281`. Note `:283-289` states the extensibility mechanism explicitly: "adding a future variation means adding a union member above and one row here, touching no JSX. `index.tsx`'s render body contains no `switch`/`if` on `props.variation` anywhere."

Derived at render (`:408-417`), NOT raw config values:
- `:408` `const hoverHidesPrice = config.hoverHidesPrice && !isUnavailable;`
- `:409` `const hoverRevealsSizeSelector = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && !isUnavailable;`
- `:410` `const sizeSelectorUnavailable = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && Boolean(isUnavailable);`
- `:417` `const bagHiddenOnMobile = config.hideBagOnMobile || (config.hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable && Boolean(isUnavailable));`
- `:381` `const showNotifyMe = Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe);`

Recipe key `:342`: `const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCard';` — consumed via `useMultiStyleConfig` (`:422-437`) with props `hoverHidesPrice`, `hoverRevealsPrice`, `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`, `sizeSelectorUnavailable`, `hoverRevealsNotifyMe`, `hideBagOnMobile`.

### Verbatim docblock quotes mentioning "Recently Viewed"

**`index.tsx:36-37`:**
> `"Recently Viewed Full History" is not a fourth variation — the AC states it behaves exactly`
> `like PLP, so callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it.`

**`index.tsx:93-95`** (inside the Badge note):
> `Per Dani Rivett's scope note on the ticket, the badge shows on PLP and Wishlist (and`

### How to add a new page route — three hard ordering constraints, all documented in-file

1. **Must precede `..._routes` if the base array also claims the path.** `:45-46`: "Must precede `..._routes` — the base array carries its own '/product/:productId' entry pointing at the base page, and `configureRoutes` keeps the first match."

A new literal route added **after** `'/:slug'` would never match — `/:slug` swallows any single-segment path. So a Full History page at e.g. `/recently-viewed` **must** be inserted before entry 6.
3. **The overrides resolver does not auto-wire pages.** `:26-32`: "The PDP override is reached through this explicit entry, not through the overrides resolver. That resolver only redirects imports that *name* `@salesforce/retail-react-app`; the base `app/routes.jsx` loads its PDP with a relative `import('./pages/product-detail')`, which is never redirected.
